title: Introduce connection-slice throttle mesh and emergency soft-rollback hotfix
author: Avery Collins
description:
Motivation: During a high-latency incident in eu-west we observed connection storms that caused abrupt circuit flips and large SLO oscillations for a subset of tenants. This PR introduces a connection-slice throttle mesh (lightweight admission layer that slices long-lived connections into bounded connection groups) and an emergency soft-rollback hook that can gracefully revert the throttle mesh state without restarting nodes.

Scope: The change adds a new connection-slice controller in the serving runtime, augments the SLO enforcer to observe slice-level load, and introduces an ops-facing hotpath to soft-rollback slice assignments when telemetry indicates regressions. The approach is designed to be conservative: slices limit concurrent fastpath reservations and favor evicting best-effort requests first. The controller is pluggable and toggled off by default for Dedicated clusters; rollout is controlled via feature flag and a short-lived config in the private installer manifest.

What this PR does (summary):
- Implement connection-slice controller with token-based slice quotas and soft-eviction policy.
- Wire slice metrics through the telemetry pipeline (slice.{utilization,evictions,avg_latency}).
- Extend the SLO enforcer to support slice-level budgets and to recommend per-tenant slice caps when backpressure triggers.
- Add an emergency soft-rollback API + ops CLI (no binary restart) to revert slice mappings and drain slices over a configurable grace window.
- Add unit + integration tests for controller invariants and a small e2e scenario that simulates a regional surge.

- unit-tests: pass

Review conversation (high level):
- Priya Natarajan: "Controller looks reasonable; concerned about eviction fairness across tenants. Please add a unit that asserts eviction order when slice budget is saturated." — Author: "Added eviction-order unit and added comments explaining tenant fairness heuristic." (commit included)
- Marcus Lee: "Telemetry looks great, but slice export cardinality could be high for large clusters. Can we limit to top N hot slices?" — Author: "Implemented sampling cap and documented the cap; default is top 500 slices by evictions across window; configurable via telemetry config." (commit included)
- Jules Park: "Ops rollback API looks powerful; ensure RBAC and audit logs are present." — Author: "Added RBAC check in soft-rollback handler and audit log entry; updated ops manifest to require management ACL." (commit included)
- SRE acceptance: After canary in a single eu-west rack (observed no SLO regression), we ran a wider canary across eu-west region with throttled ramp; telemetry graphs in docs show reduced fastpath saturation and smoother SLO quantiles.

Rollout & rollback plan: Feature gated behind feature flag runtime.conn_slice.enabled=false by default. Rollout steps documented in docs/operations/connection-slice-throttle.md — initial canary on two noncritical racks, observe slice.* metrics for 30m, then scale to region. If SLO regressions detected, ops can trigger soft-rollback via ops-cli (softrollback --manifest ops/deploy/hotfix-manifest.yaml --grace-window 120s) which will replay previous mapping and drain slices over grace window; this API is non-blocking and returns a rollback_id for audit.

Release notes (for customers): Adds an experimental connection-slicing admission controller to help stabilize regional surges; disabled by default. An ops hotfix provides safe rollback without node restarts. See docs for canary and opt-in.
